items.title: How the GNIS Lake Ontario/Lake America name change in the U.S. will appear in Maps
items.summary: The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States.

items.title: Planetary prediction engine: Automating global models via Earth AI
items.summary: Rama Pasumarthi, Staff Software Engineer, and Shravya Shetty, Distinguished Engineer, Google Research As part of Google Earth AI , we introduce the planetary prediction engine (PPE), an experimental research capability that autonomously executes the full geospatial modeling workflow — from data discovery to model training — achieving improvements across diverse prediction tasks in public health, food security, environmental risk, and socioeconomics.

items.title: Celebrate 110 years of national parks with Maps, Search, and Gemini
items.summary: What people are searching in the lead-up to National Parks Week — plus, how Ask Maps, AI Mode, and the Gemini app can help turn your wanderlust into a well-planned adventure.

items.title: Automated researchers can reliably mitigate alignment failures
items.summary: As AI begins to build itself , automating alignment research becomes increasingly important to let safety research keep pace.

items.title: TASTE: Can AI Models Judge AI Safety Research Proposals?
items.summary: We built TASTE (The AI Safety Taste Evaluation) — a benchmark measuring how well models can judge pairs of AI safety research proposals, scored by agreement with the preferences of experienced human researchers.

items.title: EU AI Act Moved Into Real Enforcement Phase: New Rules Are Already in Force
items.summary: The European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) has moved from rulemaking to real-world enforcement: as of August 2, 2026, new transparency and disclosure requirements for chatbots and AI-generated content took effect in the EU.

items.title: Colorado Unveils New Proposed Rules Implementing Revamped AI Act
items.summary: Colorado is considering new regulations to implement the state’s revamped artificial intelligence (AI) laws, which would specify requirements for the new multistage notice framework employers must follow when using AI for employment decisions beginning on January 1, 2027.
